subject: Cygnus BioSystems — custom remedy & latency SLO structure (exec approval requested)
messages:
From: Anna Morales <anna@cygnusbio.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: SLA / remedy structure for pilot — ask

Logan / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Cygnus is excited to move into a small internal pilot (1 team, ~2M tokens/month). Before legal signs the PO, procurement flagged two items: 1) a latency SLO tied to a 95th percentile 1s target for 512-token requests (our internal UX requires tight tail latency), and 2) the standard service-credit remedy in Redwood's contract assumes a 99.95% uptime SLA with quarterly credits capped at 5% of spend.

Because this pilot will run in a shared-hosted sandbox and include sensitive workflows, our security/comms team is requesting a temporary guarded SLA profile: allow an uptime target of 99.5% for the pilot term with a capped service-credit ladder (they want a hard cap of 15% of monthly spend for the pilot only). They are also asking for a stricter latency remedy (if 95th > 1.2s for two consecutive weeks, automatic routing to a higher-tier model until resolved).

I know this deviates from your standard remedies and caps. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a pilot-specific exception (30–60 day pilot) with these limits, and what discount / pricing adjustment would be required to make this commercially viable for Redwood? Attaching our procurement summary.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Morales
Head of Product Ops, Cygnus BioSystems
--

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: SLA / remedy structure for pilot — ask

Forwarding Cygnus' ask. TL;DR: customer requests a pilot-only SLA deviation — uptime 99.5% (vs our 99.95 standard) and a soft latency remediation that would automatically route to a higher-tier model when 95th percentile exceeds 1.2s for 2 weeks. They also want the quarterly credit cap raised to 15% for the pilot.

Proposed commercial trade: accept pilot concession for 45 days in exchange for a 20% pilot discount on token pricing and an explicit requirement that Cygnus run within our hosted sandbox (no private deployment). We keep the remedy ladder but change the cap only for the pilot term and require a joint post-pilot review and rollback to standard SLAs if they move to production.

Key asks for this thread: 
- Ben: operational feasibility and risk (does the auto-route remediation expose us to unbounded costs?).
- Lauren: legal redline recs for a temporary cap/termination language (we want to avoid long-term precedence).
- Marissa: pricing and exec uplift if necessary — is this a credit we can approve or do we need Jonas' signoff?

Attaching Redwood draft of temporary terms.

Thanks,
Logan
--

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLA / remedy structure for pilot — ask

Logan,

Quick operational read: the auto-route remediation is feasible if we implement a deterministic fallback policy that routes affected requests to a higher-capacity model pool for the pilot. We can throttle the duration of the fallback (e.g., 72 hours) and require manual ops confirmation for further escalation — that limits open-ended cost exposure.

However, increasing the credit cap to 15% for even a 45-day pilot is material. Worst-case we could hit that cap only if there is a prolonged outage; our historical pilot telemetry suggests that in hosted pilots the observed monthly credit liability tends to be <4% if we keep autoscaling tuned.

Operational mitigations I recommend we include in the draft:
- Fixed fallback window (72 hours) before manual ops approval.
- Explicit cost-protection clause: any monthly credits >8% trigger a joint steering call and a commercial remediation (discount clawback or shortened pilot).
- Requirement that Cygnus must run within specified regions (us-west-2) to avoid cross-region failure modes.

If Marissa/Legal are comfortable with those controls, I can sign off on the operational side.

Ben
Director, Customer Reliability

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLA / remedy structure for pilot — ask

Thanks — couple of legal points: 
1) Any temporary cap/exception must be strictly time-boxed and include explicit language that it is pilot-only and non-precedential. I propose a 60-day term with a single 30-day extension that requires Director-level (Marissa) sign-off.
2) Replace absolute percentage language with a schedule: 0–5% credits = automatic; 5–10% = remediation plan required; >10% = exec review and capped at 15% for the pilot only. That gives us a governance ladder.
3) For the latency auto-route, we need to avoid language that creates a guaranteed automatic performance uplift — keep it as an operational remediation we will attempt ("may route"). Also add a cap on remediation-triggered additional API costs (limit dollar exposure).

If those edits are OK commercially, we can bake them into the Redwood-Remedy-Terms-draft and submit to the customer.

-Lauren
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: URGENT: Exec approval needed — Cygnus pilot concession (time-limited)

Jonas —

We need your executive signoff on a one-off concession for Cygnus BioSystems (deal CYG-2027-0421). Summary: 45-day pilot, hosted sandbox only, pricing: 20% pilot discount, temporary uptime cap increased to 15% credit cap (governed by schedule and escalation thresholds), and a latency remediation that "may route" to a reserved model pool for a fixed 72-hour fallback window. Operational and legal have proposed guardrails (Ben/Lauren attached recommended edits).

Commercial considerations: the opportunity is mid-market bioscience (pilot with clear path to paid production if UX targets met). We estimate lifetime value >$250k if production follows. However, this sets a precedent risk. The controls are designed to keep financial exposure bounded and require post-pilot review.

Acceptable approval actions: 
- Approve as-is (with Ben/Lauren guardrails) — no further escalation.
- Approve with reduced discount (e.g., 10% instead of 20%).
- Deny — return to customer with standard SLA only.

Please reply with your decision by EOD PST — they are pushing for contract execution this week.

Marissa
VP, Sales

Marissa / team,

I reviewed the summary and the guardrails. Approve conditionally as follows:

- Pricing: approve 15% pilot discount (reduced from 20%).

Conditions that must be in the executed addendum: explicit non-precedent clause, region restriction (us-west-2 only), documented steering call trigger for credits >8% and joint rollback clause.

If those are included in the final addendum, Ben/Lauren you have my signoff to finalize. Marissa/Logan — proceed to redline and get customer confirmation.

Jonas
